title: Quotient-system realization and scalar Hom model of a normalized tower
statement:
theorem integralDualizing_mapping_tower_system_model
    (T : NormalizedDVRTower l E X D hl) :
    ∃ (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
      (a : ∀ n : ℕ, T.M n ≅
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q)),
      (∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
        T.tau h ≫ (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (a n).hom =
          (a m).hom ≫ (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app
            (coefTraceInput l E X Q)) ∧
      ∀ S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X,
        Nonempty (integralDualizingMappingTower l E X T.tower ≅
          (sfIntegralConstructible l E X).ι.op ⋙ coefPairingHom l E X S Q)

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: Choose Q_0 representing T.M 0. Given Q_n and its identification, represent the successor morphism T.M(n+1) to Res Q_n by a roof in the source finite coefficient category. Its left leg is a quasi-isomorphism; take its middle complex to be Q_(n+1). The right leg is a strict semilinear chain map to Q_n. Compose successors and transpose. The given finite quotient cocycle proves the evaluation comparison a commutes with every transition.

Restrict Q to completed coefficients. Its evaluated objects and transitions are those of T, by a and T.tower_tau. Apply sequentialTowerEvaluation_full to this one compatible family; all components are isomorphisms, so the resulting map of strict derived towers is an isomorphism. There is no choice of a lift varying with the input K.

For any S, sequence-site scalar internal-Hom adjunction identifies Hom(const K,Res Q) with quotient Hom(S.reduction K,Q). The unit-normalized reduction adjunction identifies S.reduction with the same scalar extension. The section-preserving equivalence and the derived section square retain the actual integral action. These comparisons commute with precomposition before localization, and hence give the natural isomorphism in the conclusion.
